technical_project:
Image Browser is my closest analogue to the Inbox Desktop App rebuild. The problem: local image libraries grow to tens of thousands of files; existing tools cannot do semantic search, and cloud alternatives either upload the library or require an account. I wanted Pinterest-style masonry browsing and a search bar that accepted natural language ("snowy mountain at sunset") or a sample image and returned matches, entirely offline.

Approach: Tauri 2 (Rust backend, React 19 frontend), three ONNX-Runtime encoders (CLIP ViT-B/32, DINOv2-Base, SigLIP-2 Base 256) running in parallel, rank lists fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack 2009, k=60), embeddings persisted in SQLite WAL via bytemuck::cast_slice. Single-flight indexing with an AtomicBool plus RAII RunningGuard so rapid filesystem events coalesce; notify watcher with 5-second debounce.

The architectural decision worth naming: the first cut used a single Mutex<Connection> for the whole DB. Under sustained ingest, the foreground ipc.get_images call blocked behind writer batches and produced a 22-second freeze. The fix was a dual-connection pattern: writer Mutex<Connection> for mutations plus a read-only secondary opened via OnceLock<Mutex<Connection>> for SELECTs. Read traffic stopped blocking behind writes.

Outcome: image-search latency under 200ms across libraries of ~10,000 images on an M2 MacBook Air, zero post-launch network traffic, freeze eliminated.
